subject: EU-West Serving Degradation: bridging steps & recovery commitment
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood-inference.com>
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@acme-retail.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood-inference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood-inference.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Apr 2027 09:12:00 +0000
Subject: EU-West Serving Degradation: bridging steps & recovery commitment

Elena / ACME ops team —

Quick update from the incident bridge: we observed elevated latency and a small spike in 5xxs for your EU-west dedicated pool starting ~08:40 UTC. Root cause is still being verified by infra but initial telemetry points to an allocator starvation combined with a high-frequency warmup storm from a small subset of tenants.

What we’ve done so far (immediate mitigations):
- Temporarily routed a fraction of your traffic to our EU-central warm standby (compatible model variant) to reduce tail latency for critical routes.
- Applied prefix-KV cache warming for your most common prompt patterns to reduce backend load.
- Enabled a transient throttling policy on bursty connections from non-critical clients.

Planned near-term actions (next 12 hours):
- Full allocator sweep and hot-queue deflation (ops in progress).
- Canary traffic ramp back to EU-west once queue depth is under target thresholds.
- We will collect a latency snapshot and a token-level cost / impact report for your review.

Commitment: we will provide a formal recovery confirmation and a short post-incident summary by EOD UTC. Where our mitigation impacted throughput (e.g., routing to EU-central), we will apply a service credit consistent with the SLA guidance.

Attachments: bridge_runbook.pdf (ops steps applied), latency_snapshot.csv (first dump)

Immediate ask from us: please confirm the critical routes you want prioritized for the EU-central routing fallback (e.g., /api/generate chat-completions). We prioritized chat-completions and streaming by default.

Thanks and very sorry for the disruption — we know this impacts user flows.

— Logan
Logan Wright
Account Lead, Strategic Customers
Redwood Inference

From: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@acme-retail.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood-inference.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Apr 2027 11:45:00 +0000
Subject: Re: EU-West Serving Degradation: bridging steps & recovery commitment

Logan —

Thanks for the quick update. We saw a noticeable latency increase on our checkout recommender endpoint (prod-reco) starting ~08:50 UTC and a small number of failed item lookups that caused a degraded user experience for a subset of EU customers. Our product team flagged increased cart drop-off during the window.

Please prioritize prod-reco and the session-embedding route. If you route to EU-central, can you confirm whether embeddings and streaming responses keep the same model variant (we have tight latency expectations for embeddings)?

Also need an ETA for a full recovery and an estimate of user requests impacted.

Elena
Elena Rossi
Director, Platform Ops — ACME Retail

Logan / Soojin / Karthik —

Forwarding ACME’s priority list. Action items we should own now:
1) Confirm model parity between EU-west and EU-central for embeddings (Karthik). If slight model mismatch, validate cost/latency impact and confirm fallback mapping.
2) Prepare a per-route affected-request estimate (engineering + telemetry). I’ll start running a lookback on 08:30–09:30 UTC and flag sessions with >200ms tail latency.
3) Prepare a short customer-facing timeline + recovery ETA for Elena — aim EOD UTC.
4) Keep the bridge open for 2 hours after routing is fully reverted.

Notes from ops: allocator sweep started at 10:05 UTC and we saw steady queue depth reduction after 11:00 UTC in the sampled hosts. However, two nodes still had delayed kernel reclamation — engineering investigating.

Marissa

From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood-inference.com>
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@acme-retail.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood-inference.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood-inference.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Apr 2027 17:58:00 +0000
Subject: Re: EU-West Serving Degradation: bridging steps & recovery commitment — post-incident summary

Elena —

Thanks for the context and for flagging prod-reco and session-embeddings. Below is a concise post-incident summary and concrete next steps. We’ll also drop the longer postmortem doc to your Drive link (attached: postmortem_summary.pdf) and the Jira for engineering work.

Summary (what happened)
- Incident start: 2027-04-30 08:40 UTC — allocator starvation in a subset of EU-west hosts combined with a short warmup storm from several tenants that caused queue buildup and higher tail latency.
- Customer impact: increased p50/p95 latency on prod-reco and session-embedding routes, and ~0.8% 5xx rate for affected calls between 08:40–11:05 UTC. We estimate ~12k user requests (ACME production) were impacted.

Immediate mitigations applied
- Partial routing to EU-central for prioritized routes (prod-reco, session-embeddings, streaming chat-completions) between 09:00–11:00 UTC — this reduced tail latency by ~65% for those routes.
- Prefix-KV warming and transient throttling for noisy upstream connections.
- Allocator sweep + kernel reclamation for two delayed hosts — completed 11:20 UTC.

Root cause (short)
- A registry bug in the allocator caused delayed reclamation under specific warmup patterns; when combined with simultaneous warmup requests from multiple tenants it led to a hot-queue.

Remediations & timeline
- Immediate: patch applied to allocator candidate during incident (hotfix) — verified on sampled hosts by 12:10 UTC.
- Mid-term: add queue-depth autoscale guard and noise-detection to prevent warmup storms (engineering ticket OP-1223).
- Long-term: model of tenant warmup behavior + automated pre-warming recommendation for heavy customers (quarterly roadmap).

Customer compensation
- We will apply a one-time service credit equivalent to 10% of April usage for the dedicated pool for the impacted period; formal credit will appear on the next invoice.

Actions for ACME (requested)
- Confirm if you want us to keep autoscale guard thresholds more conservative for your pool for the next 14 days (we can do this to avoid regressions at the cost of slightly higher baseline capacity).
- Accept the Drive postmortem link for internal review; we’ll run a joint RCA call next week if useful.

Attachments: postmortem_summary.pdf (detailed timeline + telemetry), latency_snapshot.csv (detailed per-route samples)

Again, apologies for the disruption. We’re treating this with high priority and will follow up with the RCA ticket and a planned remediation schedule.

Best —

Logan Wright
